raw.details:
About the Innovation Challenge

  • Have an idea that can solve a real-world problem? Have you developed a prototype, built a product, or imagined a solution that could make a difference?
  • The Innovation Challenge at Gwalior AI Summit 2026 invites students, researchers, aspiring entrepreneurs, and innovators to showcase their creativity, problem-solving abilities, and innovative ideas.
  • We believe innovation has no boundaries. It can begin with a simple idea, a software application, a physical product, a hardware prototype, or a completely new approach to an existing problem.
  • Whether you are building an IoT device, developing a hardware solution, designing a software platform, creating a smart product, exploring robotics, improving an existing process, or working on an entirely different innovation, we welcome you to participate.

There are no predefined domain restrictions. Bring your idea, demonstrate its potential, and show us how it can create meaningful impact.

What Can You Showcase?

We welcome innovations of all kinds, including but not limited to:

  • Software applications and digital products
  • Hardware prototypes and electronic systems
  • IoT devices and connected solutions
  • Robotics, automation, and smart systems
  • AI-powered products and intelligent solutions
  • Sustainable products and environmental innovations
  • Healthcare, agriculture, education, and community-focused solutions
  • New technologies, business models, and process improvements
  • Social innovations and solutions to everyday challenges
  • Any other original idea, product, or invention

These are examples, not restrictions. Any field, any domain, any technology — if your idea solves a problem or creates value, it belongs here.

Why Participate?

  • Cash Prizes: Compete for exciting cash prizes and recognition for outstanding innovations. Winners will be selected based on the quality, originality, feasibility, and potential impact of their work.
  • Funding Opportunities: Promising innovations may receive opportunities to connect with potential funding sources, incubation programmes, and relevant innovation ecosystem partners, subject to eligibility and availability.
  • Angel Investor Connect: Selected innovators may get opportunities to present their ideas to angel investors and explore potential investment interest.
  • Expert Evaluation and Feedback: Present your innovation to an evaluation panel and gain valuable feedback to help strengthen your idea, prototype, or product.
  • Networking and Collaboration: Connect with fellow innovators, researchers, industry professionals, entrepreneurs, and members of the startup ecosystem.
  • A Platform for Your Ideas: Showcase your work at Gwalior AI Summit 2026 and gain visibility for your innovation among a diverse community of thinkers and builders.

Who Can Participate?

The challenge is open to:

  • Undergraduate and postgraduate students
  • Research scholars and academicians
  • Individual innovators and inventors
  • Student teams and interdisciplinary groups
  • Aspiring entrepreneurs and startup founders
  • Developers, designers, engineers, and makers
  • Anyone with an innovative idea or solution who meets the official eligibility requirements

Participants from any academic discipline or technical background are encouraged to apply.

What Can You Submit?

You may present any of the following:

  • An innovative idea or concept
  • A proof of concept
  • A working prototype
  • A hardware or software product
  • A developed solution addressing a real-world problem
  • An early-stage startup idea or product
  • An improvement to an existing technology, product, or process

Your innovation does not need to be limited to AI. However, if AI is part of your solution, you are welcome to highlight how it contributes to the innovation.

Submission Guidelines

Participants should register through Unstop and submit their innovation details in the prescribed format.

Your submission should ideally cover:

  • Title of Innovation: Give your idea a clear and memorable name.
  • Problem Statement: Explain the problem or need you are addressing.
  • Proposed Innovation: Describe your idea, product, or solution.
  • Uniqueness: Explain what makes your approach different or valuable.
  • Current Development Stage: Indicate whether it is a concept, proof of concept, prototype, or developed product.
  • Working Demonstration: Include photographs, diagrams, a video, a demo link, or other supporting materials, if available.
  • Practical Impact: Explain who could benefit from your innovation and how.
  • Future Scope: Describe how your innovation could be improved, implemented, or scaled.

Participants should submit original work or clearly disclose any third-party contributions and intellectual property used.

Evaluation Criteria

Innovations may be evaluated on the following parameters:

  • Originality and creativity
  • Significance of the problem being addressed
  • Practical utility and relevance
  • Technical feasibility and quality of execution
  • Functionality and demonstration, where applicable
  • Potential for real-world impact
  • Scalability and sustainability
  • Quality of explanation and presentation

The evaluation will consider the nature and development stage of each innovation. A promising early-stage concept should be presented honestly and evaluated in the context of its maturity.

Awards and Opportunities

Outstanding innovations will be considered for:

  • Cash prizes for winning entries
  • Recognition at Gwalior AI Summit 2026
  • Potential funding and incubation connections
  • Opportunities to interact with angel investors
  • Expert feedback and innovation ecosystem networking

Funding, incubation, and investor engagement opportunities are subject to selection, availability, due diligence, and the decisions of the respective partners. Participation does not guarantee investment or funding.

Important Dates

  • Registration and submission deadline: To be announced on Unstop
  • Shortlist announcement: To be announced
  • Final presentations and awards: 29–30 October 2026
